info.name: Bifrost V1 - Virtual Key Object Ownership
info.description: client.enforce_vk_object_ownership end to end. Two virtual keys share one provider key. With the setting on, a file the owner uploads is a 404 to the other key on retrieve, download and delete and is missing from its list, while the owner still reaches it. Turned off, the other key retrieves, downloads and lists the file, and the owner uploads a second file. Turned back on, both files are a 404 to the other key and missing from its list, which shows the creator is recorded while the setting is off. Teardown deletes both files and both keys and restores the client config snapshot. Files are the probe because they are free; the same setting covers batches, videos, containers, cached contents and live sessions. Known limit: a fresh install reads back log_retention_days 0, which PUT /api/config refuses, so the snapshot raises it to 30 and Teardown restores 30. If a run is killed before Teardown and leaves ownership off, the next run's first check (enforce_vk_object_ownership is on by default) fails.
